name: Helmet Butte Standard Route
approach: From Coles Corner on US-2 (about 20 miles east of Stevens Pass), take WA-207 north 4.4 miles, turn right onto Chiwawa Loop Road for 1.3 miles, then left onto Chiwawa River Road (Forest Road 6200) and follow it roughly 23 miles to its end at the Trinity / Buck Creek Pass Trailhead (about 2,772-2,800 ft). Important: as of May 20, 2026, FR 6200 is closed to vehicle traffic beyond Atkinson Flats Campground, cutting off drive-in access to Trinity indefinitely - confirm current road status with the Wenatchee River Ranger District before relying on this approach. From the trailhead, hike the Buck Creek Trail #1513 (signed Buck Creek Pass Trail #789 on Forest Service pages), climbing steadily through forest and along Buck Creek roughly 8.8 miles to about 5,600 ft, where the standard line breaks off-trail to the right toward Pass No Pass.
itinerary: Day 1: Drive to Trinity Trailhead (FR 6200 has been closed beyond Atkinson Flat since May 20, 2026 under order 06-17-07-2026-11 - verify before departure) and backpack the ~8.8-mile approach to a camp at Pass No Pass or Buck Creek Pass, both of which have multiple established sites. Day 2: Day-scramble Helmet Butte from camp (1-2 hours round trip from Pass No Pass); many parties combine the outing with nearby Fortress Mountain or Liberty Cap given the shared approach. Break camp and hike partway or fully out. Day 2 or 3: Finish hiking out to the trailhead.

access.fees: Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful/Interagency Pass required for trailhead parking
access.rules: Group size capped at 12 (people + stock combined) inside Glacier Peak Wilderness; larger groups must split with 1-mile separation. Campfires prohibited above 3,500 ft in wilderness.
access.permit: Free, self-issue wilderness permit required at the trailhead (Glacier Peak Wilderness)
access.closures: Chiwawa River Road (FR 6200) closed beyond Atkinson Flats Campground to Trinity Trailhead since May 20, 2026 due to storm damage - confirm current status with the Wenatchee River Ranger District before driving. The Little Giant Fire closure (order 06-17-07-2026-40), in effect September 3 through October 31, 2026 unless lifted sooner, also closes FR 6200 and the Buck Creek Trail.
access.landManager: Glacier Peak Wilderness spans the Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Darrington Ranger District, west/north side) and Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (east side); the Trinity/Buck Creek Pass approach is managed by the Wenatchee River Ranger District
access.land_manager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Wenatchee River Ranger District)
access.parking_pass: Northwest Forest Pass required at the Trinity Trailhead — $5/day or $30/year.

overnight_permit.what: Free self-issue Glacier Peak Wilderness permit
overnight_permit.where: Fill one out at the trailhead kiosk and carry it with you.

road.name: Chiwawa River Road (Forest Road 6200)
road.status: Closed beyond Atkinson Flats Campground to Trinity since May 20, 2026 due to storm damage, under Forest Service order 06-17-07-2026-11, which runs through December 31, 2027; the Little Giant Fire closure (order 06-17-07-2026-40), in effect from September 3 through October 31, 2026 unless lifted sooner, also closes the Chiwawa River Road and Buck Creek Trail #1513
road.driveNote: From Coles Corner take WA-207 N 4.4 mi, right onto Chiwawa Loop Road 1.3 mi, left onto Chiwawa River Road/FR 6200, then ~23 mi to the Trinity/Buck Creek Pass Trailhead
road.seasonalGate: Even when open, the road is a long gravel/paved Forest Service road not plowed in winter; verify current Forest Service alerts before any trip
